clue.text: Reproducing a pedigree

definitions.meaning: producing offspring, as farmers do with livestock
good lineage or ancestry, as in a person of fine family

explanation.surface: Producing young from a pedigree animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the act of raising young animals and the refined upbringing or ancestry a person inherits.

clue.text: Read it out, darling

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the word read are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone asks a loved one to read something aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges READ; 'it' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, used in direct address like sweetheart.

clue.text: Likely to be held responsible

definitions.meaning: apt or probable, as in prone to happen
legally answerable for something, such as a debt

explanation.surface: Someone is probably going to be blamed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both prone or apt to happen and legally answerable, as for damages.

clue.text: Fruit is no good as pudding!

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
duff is British slang for useless or worthless

explanation.surface: A complaint that the fruit is unfit to serve as dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A PLUM DUFF is a traditional British boiled suet pudding with raisins; DUFF is British slang for faulty or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum duff is a steamed or boiled suet dessert with dried fruit, so it is one kind of pudding.

clue.text: They're revered by crowds — case dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed suggests the words crowds and case are sent off and broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A court case thrown out, with crowds watching respectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' rearranges CROWDS plus CASE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindu cattle are held sacred, and by extension the idiom names any institution or belief exempt from criticism.

clue.text: Led into old Spanish city

parts.note: into can mean to, as in going into or to town

explanation.surface: Someone was guided into an ancient city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in the order TO, LED, O even though the clue gives Led first.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famed for its swords and its cathedral.

clue.text: Well made by eccentric English artisan

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A water well dug by an odd English craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges E plus ARTISAN; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian source is a bored shaft where water rises under its own pressure, a particular type of water source.

clue.text: Nothing if not cross when having to fill in

definitions.meaning: zero, a figure of no value

definitions.text: if not cross when having to fill in
definitions.meaning: in the game played on a three-by-three grid, a player who is not marking X fills in a circle

explanation.surface: Someone is calm about having to stand in for a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means zero, and is also the circle mark that the non-X player draws in the classic grid game.

clue.text: Go ahead, like a well-controlled dog?

definitions.meaning: to take the front position and guide others
a dog kept on a leash is restrained, with the phrase read literally

explanation.surface: An instruction to proceed, likened to an obedient pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means take the front and guide; read literally it describes a pet held on its leash.

clue.text: Somewhat strange to build such a dam

indicators.note: somewhat suggests only part of the word, so the synonym is trimmed at its end

explanation.surface: It seems odd to construct this kind of barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' trims WEIRD to its first four letters; 'to build' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A low barrier across a river that raises the water level is a type of dam.

clue.text: Scream "obscene to kill!" — what a din!

parts.note: blue means indecent or risque, as in a blue joke

explanation.surface: Someone yells about an indecent killing over a loud noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scream' sets up the idiom 'scream blue murder', meaning to make a great fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an uproar or terrific racket, as in screaming at the top of one's voice.

clue.text: Old reaper got ill, left halfway through

indicators.note: halfway through keeps only the first half of the word left

explanation.surface: An elderly farmhand fell sick and departed midway through the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfway through' keeps LE from 'left'; 'got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved hand blade used for cutting grain is a traditional harvesting tool, an old-fashioned cutter.

clue.text: A winger Australians consider laughable?

parts.note: a winger here is a bird, and the Australian species is known for a call like human laughter

explanation.surface: A sports winger whom Australians find ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Australian kingfisher is called the laughing jackass for its cackling cry.

clue.text: Elvis hit an animal

definitions.meaning: a 1956 number one record by Elvis Presley

explanation.surface: Elvis struck a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a 1956 Presley single is also a term for a hunting canine.

clue.text: He sounds like the coarser kind of tradesman

indicators.note: sounds like says the synonym is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: grosser means coarser or more vulgar

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who seems more vulgar than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' signals that GROSSER said aloud gives the answer; 'He' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling food and household goods is one type of retailer.

clue.text: Deb came right out and got hugged

indicators.note: out here means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A debutante appeared and received a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DEB, CAME and R; 'and got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone closely in one's arms is to clasp them, a synonym.

clue.text: Find money for a fine car

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Raising cash to buy an excellent motor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to pay for something means having the means to buy it.

clue.text: Rows, a bit of a ding-dong all round — altogether stupefying!

indicators.note: all round places the outer word around the inner one

parts.note: ding is the first part of ding-dong

explanation.surface: Quarrels and a noisy fight leave everyone dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' puts the first part of 'ding-dong' around the quarrels. 'Rows' looks like a synonym to swap but is used as written; 'altogether' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming sluggish and half-asleep is a dazed, torpid state, close to being stupefied.

clue.text: Clergyman is at first eager to make changes

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

indicators.note: at first selects the opening letter of the word eager

explanation.surface: A minister is keen at the outset to bring in reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes E from 'eager'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend or rework something, such as a text, is to alter it.

clue.text: Unseemly struggle during game

definitions.meaning: a word-building board game with lettered tiles

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a messy scramble and is also the name of a board game with lettered tiles.

clue.text: Young birds' curious mode of speech

indicators.note: curious suggests something odd is done to the word speech, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chicks have a strange way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious mode of' rearranges SPEECH. The definition reads with 'speech' in the surface: what chicks utter.
explanation.definitionFit: Short high-pitched calls are the sounds made by fledglings and chicks.

clue.text: English spa in Massachusetts

definitions.meaning: A village in West Yorkshire, England
the state capital and largest city of Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A spa town from England located in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a Yorkshire spa village and to the capital of Massachusetts.

clue.text: That sausage is an absolute cracker!

definitions.meaning: a firework that goes off with a loud bang

explanation.surface: Praise for a superb sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a sausage, which bursts when fried, is also a noisy firework.

clue.text: Control, for example, in a sport that's in a lot of trouble

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another here

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of in a lot are jumbled

explanation.surface: Governing a sport that is in serious difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the example abbreviation inside the rugby code; 'of trouble' rearranges the letters of IN A LOT for the second half. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or restriction imposed by authority is a means of governing conduct.

clue.text: Meat dish is hot as hot can be!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A meal served piping hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'as hot as can be' hides the pieces H, AS, H; 'is' and 'can be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of chopped cooked meat fried with potatoes is a classic leftover meal.

clue.text: Has good implant to offer ugly old women

indicators.note: implant means to set one thing inside another

explanation.surface: Someone has a good implant to give to unattractive elderly women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implant' puts G inside HAS; 'to offer' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory term for unattractive elderly females, like crones or witches.

clue.text: In madras, Parsees are thin on the ground

indicators.note: In tells the solver that the letters lie inside the words madras Parsees

explanation.surface: Parsis are few in the Indian city of Madras.
explanation.walkthrough: MADRAS, now Chennai, is a city in India; Parsees are Zoroastrians of Persian descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scattered and scarce is meagre in number or spread out.

clue.text: Appearing because a letter is urgent, one's told

indicators.note: one is told, meaning the solver hears these words spoken

parts.note: the letter M, spelt out as em, followed by urgent

explanation.surface: Something shows up because a message is pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, the letter M and 'urgent' run together; 'because' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming into being or becoming visible, like a new nation or trend that is arising.
